The progenitor of all Buddhas, the supreme son of the Buddha,
born from the source of wisdom, the womb, the womb of Dharma, and the bringer of an end to existence.
The solid essence of the single [reality], having the nature of a vajra, the newly born Lord of the World;
arisen from space, self-existent, the great fire of the wisdom of insight.
Vairocana, the great radiance; the illuminator of the light of gnosis;
the lamp of the world; the torch of gnosis; the one of great splendor; the self-luminous.
King of Vidyās, supreme lord of mantras, king of mantras who accomplishes the great purpose;
Great Uṣṇīṣa, wondrous Uṣṇīṣa, all-seeing lord of the sky.
The foremost embodiment of all Buddhas, whose eyes bring joy to the world,
the creator of manifold forms, he is the venerable and worshipful Great Sage.
The mantra-practitioner upholds the three families, maintains the great samaya-mantra,
bears the Three Jewels as supreme, and is the excellent teacher of the highest of the three vehicles.
Amoghapāśa, the victorious one, Vajrapāśa, the great seizer;
Vajrāṅkuśa, the great noose, and Vajrabhairava, the terrifier.
Thus end the twenty-four and a quarter verses on the Wisdom of the Perfectly Pure Dharmadhātu.
The King of Wrath is six-faced, terrifying, six-eyed, six-armed, and powerful;
he has formidable fangs, is skeletal, is Halāhala, and possesses a hundred faces.
Yamāntaka, King of Obstacles, Vajravega, Terrifier,
Resounding Vajra, Heart-Vajra, Illusion-Vajra, and Mahodara.
Lord of the thunderbolt, born from the vajra, the vajra-maṇḍala, resembling the sky;
possessing the majesty of a single unmoving matted lock of hair, he wears a moist elephant hide as a garment.
The cry of "hā hā" is most terrible; the cry of "hī hī" is fearsome;
the "aṭṭahāsa" laugh, the great laugh, the "vajra-laugh," and the great roar.
Vajrasattva, the Great Being; Vajra King, the Great Bliss;
Vajra Caṇḍa, the Great Joy; Vajra Hūṃkāra, the Utterer of Hūṃ.
Bearing the weapon of the vajra-arrow, the vajra-sword that severs;
the bearer of the universal vajra, the wielder of the vajra, the sole vajra-wielder who abandons strife.
His eyes are formidable with vajra-flames, and his hair is vajra-flames;
he is the vajra-penetration, the great penetration, the hundred-eyed one, and the vajra-eyed one.
His body consists of sprouts of vajra-hair; his singular form is composed of vajra-hair;
he has the onset of vajra-tips as his nails; and his skin is dense with the essence of the vajra.
The glorious bearer of the vajra-garland, adorned with vajra ornaments,
whose roar is the great laugh "Hā hā," the sound of the vajra, the six-syllabled one.
Mañjughoṣa, the great roar, the single sound of the three worlds, the great;
his voice extends to the limits of the realm of space, he is the best among those who possess a voice.
Thus, there are ten verses on the mirror-like wisdom, including one verse:
"Suchness, true selflessness, the limit of reality, and the letterless;
the bull among proponents of emptiness, whose roar is profound and vast. (BuSto 108.77)
The great-sounding conch of Dharma, the great drum of Dharma,
the unestablished nirvāṇa, the drum of Dharma resounding in the ten directions.
Formless yet possessing form, the foremost, manifold in form and mind-made,
the glory that illuminates all forms, he who bears every reflection without exception.
Invincible, known as the Great Lord, the sovereign of the three realms;
established upon the exalted Noble Path, he is the banner of Dharma and the great prosperity.
He whose body is the sole youth of the three worlds, yet is ancient and venerable, a lord of creatures;
he who bears the thirty-two marks, is lovely, and is the most beautiful in the three worlds.
The teacher of the qualities of worldly knowledge, the teacher of the world, the fearless one;
the protector, the savior, the friend of the three worlds, the refuge, the unsurpassed deliverer.
He enjoys the full expanse of the sky, an ocean of the wisdom of omniscience;
he shatters the shell of the egg of ignorance and rends asunder the cage of existence.
Having pacified all afflictions and crossed to the further shore of the ocean of saṃsāra,
he bears the crown of the empowerment of primordial wisdom and is adorned with the ornaments of perfect buddhahood.

He is the pacifier of the suffering of the three types of suffering, the end of the three realms, and the infinite; he has attained the three liberations, is freed from all obscurations, and has reached equality with space.
Transcending the stains of all afflictions, he has reached the state beyond the three times;
he is the great elephant among all beings, the crest-jewel upon the crowns of all virtues.
Completely liberated from all substrates of existence, well-established in the path of space,
the Lord is the bearer of the great wish-fulfilling gem, the supreme among all jewels.
He is a vast and flourishing great wish-fulfilling tree, the supreme and excellent great auspicious vase;
he is the performer of the welfare of all sentient beings, a benefactor who desires their well-being and is compassionate toward all beings.
He knows the auspicious and the inauspicious; he knows the time, he knows the occasion, and he is the omnipresent Lord of the occasion.
He knows the faculties of sentient beings, he knows the proper moment, and he is skilled in the three liberations.
He is possessed of virtues, a knower of virtues, a knower of the Dharma, praised, and the source of auspiciousness;
he is the most auspicious of all auspicious things, and is fame, fortune, glory, and goodness.
He is the great festival, the great relief, the great bliss, and the great delight;
he is honor, veneration, prosperity, joy, glory, and the lord of fame.
The one to be chosen, the giver of boons, the most excellent, the worthy refuge, the supreme sanctuary,
the enemy of great fear, the most preeminent, and the destroyer of every trace of fear.
He has a crest, he wears a topknot, he has matted locks, he is shaggy-haired, he is shaven-headed, and he wears a diadem;
he is five-faced, he has five tufts of hair, and his crown is adorned with five rags.
Wearing the great vow, with a girdle of muñja grass, a celibate student of the highest discipline,
a great ascetic devoted to austerity, a bath-graduate, Gautama was the foremost leader.
The knower of Brahman is the Brāhmaṇa; he is Brahmā, having attained the nirvāṇa of Brahman.
He is liberation, release, the limb of liberation, emancipation, peace, and the auspicious.
Nirvāṇa, cessation, peace, the supreme good, departure, the end; it is the maker of an end to pleasure and pain, the ultimate goal, dispassion, and the destruction of the substrata of existence.
Unconquered, incomparable, unmanifest, without appearance,
stainless, partless, all-pervading, omnipresent, subtle, the seed, and untainted.
Free from dust, stainless, immaculate, with faults cast out and free from ailment;
perfectly awakened, one whose self is fully enlightened, the all-knowing, the supreme among all who know.
Transcending the nature of consciousness, wisdom bears a non-dual form;
it is free from conceptual construction, effortless, and performs the work of the Buddhas of the three times.
The Buddha is without beginning or end, the primordial Buddha, devoid of causal succession;
he is the stainless single eye of gnosis, the embodiment of gnosis, the Tathāgata.
Lord of Speech, great debater, king of speakers, bull among debaters;
best of those who speak, most excellent, lion of speakers, unconquered.
Samantadarśin, Prāmodya, Tejomālī, Sudarśana, Śrīvatsa, Suprabha, Dīpti, and Bhābhāsurakaradyuti.
The supreme and most excellent great physician, the peerless remover of thorns;
the tree of all medicines without exception, the great enemy of the disease of the afflictions.
The beloved ornament of the three worlds, glorious, a mandala of stars,
reaching to the limits of the sky in the ten directions, he is the great, lofty banner of the Dharma.
Universally vast as the sole umbrella over the world, the mandala of loving-kindness and compassion;
the glorious Padmanṛtyeśvara, the great all-pervading lord Ratnacchatra.
The great king of all buddhas, who maintains the embodiment of all buddhas;
the great yoga of all buddhas, the sole teaching of all buddhas.
The glory of the Vajra-jewel initiation, the sovereign lord of all jewels,
the lord of all lords of the world, the supreme master of all holders of the vajra.
The great mind of all Buddhas, the movement of the minds of all Buddhas,
the great body of all Buddhas, and the eloquence of all Buddhas.
The great light of the Vajra-Sun, possessing the stainless radiance of the Vajra-Moon;
the great passion beginning with dispassion, blazing with the splendor of all colors.
The Perfectly Awakened One sits in the vajra posture; he upholds the Dharma of the Buddha’s assembly.
He is the glorious one born from the lotus of the Buddhas, the bearer of the treasury of omniscient wisdom.
The King who holds the universal illusion, the great master of the Buddhas' vidyā;
the Vajra-Sharp One, the Great Sword, the utterly pure, the supreme syllable.
He who wields the great weapon of the Vajra-Dharma of the Mahāyāna that severs suffering;
Jinajik, profound as a vajra, possessing vajra-intelligence, and knowing things as they truly are.
The fulfillment of all perfections, the ornament of all stages,
possessing the purity of the selflessness of phenomena, with the light of perfect wisdom as his heart’s radiance.
The great exertion of the Net of Illusion, the supreme sovereign of all tantras;
he who sits upon the vajra-throne in its entirety, and who sustains the body of inexhaustible gnosis.
Samantabhadra, the one of excellent intelligence, Kṣitigarbha, the sustainer of the world,
the great womb of all Buddhas, and the beholder of the wheel of universal emanations.
The pinnacle of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena, the upholder of the intrinsic nature of all phenomena;
the unarisen reality, the universal purpose, the upholder of the intrinsic nature of all dharmas.
Possessing great wisdom in a single instant, he upholds the realization of all phenomena;
he is the perfect comprehension of all dharmas, the Sage who has reached the limit of reality, and the one of supreme intelligence.
Stable, with a perfectly serene mind, he upholds the awakening of the Samyaksaṃbuddhas;
he is manifest before all Buddhas, a flame of wisdom, most brilliantly radiant.
Thus are the forty-two verses on the wisdom of discernment:
The supreme accomplisher of desired aims, the purifier of all miserable rebirths,
the protector who is the highest among all beings, the liberator of all beings.

The sole hero in the battle against the afflictions, the destroyer of the pride of the enemy that is ignorance; the glorious one who wears the ornament of wisdom, yet assumes a form both heroic and loathsome.
He dances with the casting of hundreds of staff-like arms and the planting of his feet;
he dances across the expanse of the sky with the extension of his glorious hundred arms.
He stands with the entire circle of the earth beneath the sole of one foot,
and he stands with the peak of the universe beneath the nail of his big toe.
The single meaning is the meaning of non-dual phenomena; it is the ultimate reality, indestructible.
It is the object of various representations, the continuity of mind and consciousness.
One who possesses supreme wisdom finds delight in the meaning of all things without exception, and finds delight in emptiness.
And having transcended attachment to existence and so forth, he possesses the great delight of the three realms of existence.
Pure, white as a bright cloud, with a radiance like the rays of the autumn moon;
possessing the luster of the orb of the rising sun, and the brilliance of great red-colored nails.
With a sublime crest like the top of a sapphire, bearing hair as dark as a great blue gem,
possessing the splendor of the radiance of a great jewel, he is adorned with the nirvāṇa of the Buddhas.
He causes a hundred world-systems to tremble; he possesses the great stride of the bases of miraculous power.
He is the bearer of great mindfulness, the reality itself, and the sovereign of the fourfold mindfulness and meditative concentration.
He is the fragrance of the flowers of the factors of enlightenment, an ocean of the qualities of the Tathāgatas;
he knows the method of the eightfold path and knows the path of perfect awakening.
He has great attachment for all sentient beings, yet is free from attachment like the sky;
he is born from the minds of all sentient beings and possesses the speed of the minds of all sentient beings.
He knows the faculties and objects of all sentient beings; he captivates the minds of all sentient beings.
He knows the reality of the meaning of the five aggregates; he maintains the purity of the five aggregates.
Abiding at the limit of all deliverance, skilled in all deliverance;
abiding on the path of all deliverance, the teacher of all deliverance.
He has uprooted existence through its twelve links, maintains the purity of the twelve aspects,
possesses the form of the method of the four truths, and maintains the realization of the eight knowledges.
He whose meaning of the truths consists of twelve aspects, who knows reality in sixteen aspects,
whose awakening has twenty aspects— he is the fully awakened one, the supreme omniscient one.
He manifests millions of emanation bodies of immeasurable Buddhas;
he is the realization of all moments [of existence] and knows the meaning of every moment of mind.
He manifests the welfare of the world through the various vehicles, methods, and means;
having emerged from the three vehicles, he abides in the fruit of the single vehicle.
His self is purified of the element of afflictions; he brings about the exhaustion of the element of karma;
he has crossed over the ocean of the floods and has emerged from the wilderness of yoga.
Having utterly abandoned the afflictions, secondary afflictions, and all defilements along with their habitual tendencies,
he accomplishes the welfare of the world through wisdom, skillful means, and great compassion, never in vain.
He has abandoned all conceptualizations for the sake of [liberation], he is the object of consciousness, and he effects cessation;
he is the domain of the minds of all sentient beings and the movement of the minds of all sentient beings.
Abiding within the minds of all sentient beings, having attained equality with their thoughts,
he gladdens the minds of all sentient beings and brings joy to the minds of all sentient beings.
The established doctrine is free from delusion, devoid of all error,
characterized by a doubtless mind, possessing three purposes, encompassing all objects, and consisting of the three qualities.
The meaning of the five aggregates, existing in the three times, he who manifests all moments,
perfectly awakened in a single moment, and who upholds the essential nature of all Buddhas.
He whose body is bodiless, the supreme body, the one who manifests the pinnacle of bodies;
he who displays all forms without exception, the great jewel with the crest of jewels.
Thus are the twenty-four verses on the gnosis of equality:
"The unsurpassed awakening of the Buddha is that which all perfectly awakened ones have realized;
it is without syllables, the source of mantras, the great mantra, and the three families."
The great bindu, which is without syllables, gives rise to the meaning of all mantras;
it is the five-syllabled great emptiness, the bindu-emptiness, and the six-syllabled.
Possessing all forms yet formless, holding the sixteen, the half, and the quarter-bindu;
partless, beyond calculation, he holds the pinnacle of the fourth dhyāna.
He is the master of all the arts of meditative concentration, the knower of the lineage and clan of samādhis;
he is the body of samādhi, the supreme among bodies, and the sovereign of all saṃbhogakāyas.
The Emanation Body is the foremost of bodies, upholding the lineage of the Buddha’s emanations;
manifesting as various emanations throughout the ten directions, it accomplishes the welfare of the world according to what is appropriate.
The god beyond gods, the lord of gods, the lord of the Suras, the sovereign of the Dānavas;
the lord of the immortals, the preceptor of the gods, the Pramatha, the lord of the Pramathas.
Having crossed the wilderness of existence, he alone is the Teacher, the Guru of the world;
his fame pervades the ten directions, and he is the great lord of the gift of Dharma.
Girt with the armor of loving-kindness, clad in the mail of compassion,
bearing the sword of wisdom and the bow and arrows, he abandons the battle against afflictions and ignorance.
The enemy of Māra, the conqueror of Māra, the hero who brings an end to the fear of the four Māras;
the victor over the entire host of Māras, the bound one, the leader of the world.
He is to be revered, worshipped, saluted, and honored at all times;
he is the most worthy of adoration, the one to be esteemed, the one to be prostrated to—the supreme Guru.
His stride traverses the three worlds alone, and his prowess extends to the limits of space;
he is learned in the three Vedas, a master of sacred scripture, purified, possessed of the six superknowledges, and endowed with the six recollections.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva has transcended the world and possesses great supernatural power;
he is established in the perfection of wisdom and has attained the very nature of wisdom.
The knower of self and the knower of others, he is all and the most excellent; for he is the foremost of persons, transcending all comparisons, the supreme lord of knowledge.
The master of the gift of Dharma is supreme, the teacher of the meaning of the four mudrās;
he is most worthy of being venerated by the worlds of those who proceed toward the three vehicles of liberation.
The glory of ultimate purity, the great one who brings fortune to the three worlds,
the creator of all prosperity, the glorious Mañjuśrī, the best among the glorious.
Thus end the fifteen verses on the knowledge of performing duties.
Homage to you, O bestower of boons, O supreme vajra, O limit of reality; let there be homage to you.
Homage to you, whose womb is emptiness, O awakening of the Buddhas; let there be homage to you.
O passion for the Buddha, homage be to you; O desire for the Buddha, salutations again and again.
O joy in the Buddha, homage be to you; O delight in the Buddha, salutations again and again.
O Buddha-smile, homage to you; O Buddha-laughter, homage, homage! O Buddha-speech, homage to you; O Buddha-nature, homage, homage!
Homage to you, the source of non-existence; homage to you, born from the Buddha.
Homage to you, born from space; homage to you, born from primordial wisdom.
Homage to you, O Net of Illusion; homage to you, the Buddha’s drama!
Homage to you who are all things for all; homage be to you, the Body of Gnosis!
